Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we lock in the trial: 

Recap / primary goals
- Evaluate Redwood inference for Acme's customer support summarization pipeline (latency and fidelity).
- Success criteria: average response latency <= 400ms at p95, summary accuracy >= 88% on the rubric, and <3% hallucination rate on the sample corpus.

Proposed POC structure
- Week 0: dataset & security onboarding (SDR/data transfer + NDA/comms)
- Week 1: offline evals — run curated sample set through Redwood, grade with rubric (automated scoring + human spot checks)
- Week 2: online shadowing — Redwood in shadow mode behind Acme infra (no customer-facing outputs) to measure latency/throughput under realistic load
- Acceptance: pass thresholds for latency and rubric score, and no major security blockers.

Ownership
- Acme: Ava (data lead) — provide sample dataset, mapping to fields, and test keys
- Redwood: Dylan (SE) — run eval harness, provide rubric, and configure shadowing; Marissa (AM) — program-level coordination; Rachel (PM) — telemetry/SLA definitions

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf (proposal + runbook stub)

Please confirm the owners and whether the success criteria look good. If so, we can schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday to align on dataset transfer and security checklist.

Thanks,

Thanks Samir — attaching the rubric and a short methodology note. See acme-eval-rubric.xlsx attached. High level: 

Offline eval (week 1) — what we do
- You provide ~2k labeled examples (or a representative sample + labeling guidance). We run Redwood locally in our env on the sample set and output structured scoring (precision/recall on key fields, ROUGE/F1 variants for summarization).
- Hallucination detection: we run a combination of token-overlap checks, slot-validation rules (where possible), and a small human-spot-check sample (20–30 examples) to estimate hallucination rate.
- Automated scoring pipeline outputs a CSV with per-example scores and an overall pass/fail per threshold.

Online shadow (week 2) — what we measure
- Shadow traffic for 48–72 hours at target concurrency (we'll coordinate a representative load window). Measure p95 latency, tail behavior, and throughput 
- Capture token-level cost metrics and tokenization differences so you get a full cost/latency tradeoff report.

Suggested pass thresholds (can be tuned):
- p95 latency <= 400ms
- Rubric score >= 88% (weighted by precision on key fields)
- Hallucination rate <= 3% on spot-check sample

Runbook & infra notes
- We require a secure S3 bucket cross-account for sample dataset or a temporary signed transfer link; dataset should be anonymized when possible.
- We'll provide a small eval harness (Python scripts) and the rubric in the attached xlsx.

ETA for deliverables
- I can run the offline eval within 3 business days of receiving the dataset and runbook.

Attachments: acme-eval-rubric.xlsx

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the rubric next week.
